<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par53 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=6}} (see above, g) is a mere error of the scribe, who had the Aramaic form in mind and corrected it by prefixing {{GHGheb|text=ה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|q}}
7. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} the characteristic {{GHGheb|text=ה}} is regularly elided after the preformatives, thus {{GHGheb|text=יַקְטִיל}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַקְטִיל}}; but it is retained in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} after prepositions, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְהַקְטִיל}}. The exceptions are in the imperfect, {{GHGheb|text=יְהוֹשִׁיעַ|translate=He will save}} for {{GHGheb|text=יוֹשִׁיעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=47}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=6}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}}); {{GHGheb|text=יְהוֹדֶה|translate=He will praise}} for {{GHGheb|text=יוֹדֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=11|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=28|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=18|hidebook=1}} (cf. the proper name {{GHGheb|text=יְהוּכַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=3}}, for which {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=1|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=יוּכַל}} [and {{GHGheb|text=יְהוֹסֵף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=81|verse=6}}]); [{{GHGheb|text=יְהֵילִילוּ}} ({{GHGpar|70|d}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=5}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְהָתֵ֫לּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּהָתֵ֫לּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=9}}] and {{GHGheb|text=מְהֻקְצָעוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=22}}; in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} (where, however, as in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGpar|51|l}}, the {{GHGterm|infinitive Qal}} is generally to be read) {{GHGheb|text=לַסְתִּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=15}} for {{GHGheb|text=לְהַסְתִּיר}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַנְפִּל}} and {{GHGheb|text=לַצְבּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַֽעֲבִיר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַֽהֲלִק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַֽחֲטִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַלְבֵּן}} (doubly anomalous for {{GHGheb|text=לְהַלְבִּין}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=35}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַשְׁמִעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=26|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַֽאֲדִיב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=33}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַשְׁמִד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְלַשְׁבִּית}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=8|verse=4}} (certainly corrupt); {{GHGheb|text=בָּעִיר}} for {{GHGheb|text=בְּהָעִיר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=20}} (but ''in the city'' is probably meant); {{GHGheb|text=לָבִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=39|verse=7}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=10}}); {{GHGheb|text=לַמְרוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַנְחוֹתָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=כַּנְּלוֹת}} (see, however, {{GHGpar|20|h}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַרְאֹֽתְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=33}}: cf. further, from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=27|verse=20}}; on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=26|verse=12}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=10|verse=39}}, see above, k; for {{GHGheb|text=לַמְחוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=3}} read {{GHGheb|text=לְמֹחוֹת}} or {{GHGheb|text=לִמְמַחוֹת}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|r}}
8. With regard to the tone it is to be observed that the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} in Hiphʿîl have ''not'' the tone, even in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} with ''waw consecutive'' (except in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=33}} before {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=15|verse=29}} before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, to avoid a hiatus); but the plural ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} (see {{GHGpar|47|m}}) always has the tone, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּקְרִב֫וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=17}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|s}}
9. The passive (Hophʿal) has ''ŭ'' instead of Qameṣ ḥaṭuph in the first syllable ({{GHGheb|text=הֻקְטַל}}), in the strong verb less frequently in the perfect and infinitive, but generally in the participle, through the influence of the initial {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=מָשְׁחָת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=26}}); e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֻשְׁכַּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=32}} (beside {{GHGheb|text=הָשְׁכְּבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=19|hidebook=1}}); {{GHGheb|text=הֻשְׁלַךְ}} {{GHGterm|impf.}} {{GHGheb|text=יֻשְׁלַךְ}}, ''part.'' {{GHGheb|text=מֻשְׁלָךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=21}} (beside {{GHGheb|text=הָשְׁלַכְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=19}}) {{GHGheb|text=הֻמְלַ֫חַתְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}}; in the partic. Hoph. without elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}: {{GHGheb|text=מְהֻקְצָעוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=22}}; on the other hand, verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}} always have ''ŭ'' (in a sharpened syllable): {{GHGheb|text=הֻגַּד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֻגַּד}} (cf. {{GHGpar|9|n}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|t}}
10. The {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} has in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} (as in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}) {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} in the last syllable, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הָחְתֵּל}} and {{GHGheb|text=הָמְלֵחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֻגֵּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=24}}. An {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} does not occur in the strong verb.

11. With regard to the {{GHGterm|imperative Hophʿal}}, see above, {{GHGpar|46|a}}, note.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|u}}
12. According to Böttcher ({{GHGcite|title=Ausführliches Lehrbuch}}, § 906) and Barth (see above, {{GHGpar|52|e}}) a number of supposed imperfects Hophʿal are, in fact, imperfects of the passive of {{GHGterm|Qal}}. As in the case of the perfects passive of Qal (see above, {{GHGpar|52|e}}) the question is again of verbs of which neither the corresponding causative (i.e. here the Hiphʿîl), nor the other tense of the same conjugation (i.e. here the perfect Hophʿal) is found; so with {{GHGheb|text=יֻקַּם}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יֻנְקַם}}, cf. ''yuqtălŭ'' as imperfect Qal in Arabic) and {{GHGheb|text=יֻתַּן}}, from {{GHGheb|text=נָקַם}} and {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֻקַּח}} from {{GHGheb|text=לָקַח}} (cf. {{GHGpar|66|g}}); {{GHGheb|text=יוּאָר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=6}} from {{GHGheb|text=אָרַר}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֻחַן}} from {{GHGheb|text=חָנַן}}; {{GHGheb|text=יוּשָּׁ֑ד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=14}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=1}}) from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁדַד}}; Barth adds the verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}: {{GHGheb|text=תֻּתַּשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=19|verse=12}} from {{GHGheb|text=נתשׁ}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֻתָּץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lev|chapter=11|verse=35}} from {{GHGheb|text=נתץ}}; the verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}: {{GHGheb|text=יֻחָ֫קוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=23}} from {{GHGheb|text=חקק}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֻכַּת}} &c. from {{GHGheb|text=כּתת}}; the verb {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}: {{GHGheb|text=יוּדַשׁ}} from {{GHGheb|text=דּוּשׁ}}; the verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}}: {{GHGheb|text=יוּחָ֫ל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יוּשַׁר}}, {{GHGheb|text=יוּשַׁת}} from {{GHGheb|text=חִיל}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר}} and {{GHGheb|text=שִׁית}}. On {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫ישֶׂם}} &c., {{GHGpar|73|f}}. In point of fact it would be very strange, especially in the case of {{GHGheb|text=יֻתַּן}} and {{GHGheb|text=יֻקַּח}}, that of these frequently used verbs,<section end=par53 /><noinclude>
